t: Herat was first recorded under the Achaemenid Empire as the chief town of the district of Haraiva, and it passed to Alexander, the Parthian and Sasanian empires, the Arabs, the Saffarids, the Samanids, the Ghaznavids, the Seljuk Empire, the Ghurids and the Khwarazm Empire.

The Mongols besieged it twice, in the second siege ending its life as a great city for a time, and under the Timurids, above all Shah Rukh and Husayn Bayqara, it became the capital of an empire and a centre of art and learning.
After the Safavids it was ruled by Afghan tribes, was independent for a time in the 19th century, was attacked by Iran several times, and was joined to Afghanistan in 1863.
dyk: In 1979 Herat had about 140,000 people, and today it has an estimated 673,273 settled residents.
ev: Alexander the Great captures the Arian capital, Artacoana, and rebuilds the town and builds the citadel
Hephthalites and Turks fight the Arab forces in the battle of Qohestan and are defeated
Ghiyasuddin Ghori builds the great mosque of Herat
The Mongols take Herat after a second siege lasting seven months
Timur takes Herat and soon afterwards ends the Kartid dynasty
Husayn Bayqara begins his rule of Herat, which lasts until 1506
The Abdali Afghans of the city revolt and found the Sadozai Sultanate of Herat
Afghanistan conquers Herat under Dost Muhammad Khan

f.founded: The precise date of foundation is unknown. The city is first recorded under the Achaemenid Empire (550 to 330 BCE), when the district was called Haraiva. The 14th-century writer Hamdallah Mustawfi said that a chief named Herat, a follower of the hero Nariman, first founded it, and that Alexander the Great rebuilt it after it had fallen to ruin.
f.where: South of the Paropamisus Mountains, in the fertile valley of the Hari River, in western Afghanistan, on the roads to Iran and Turkmenistan.
f.known: The Achaemenid district of Haraiva; Alexander's Artacoana; the Ghurid great mosque of 1201; the two Mongol sieges; the Kartid dynasty; the Timurid capital of Shah Rukh and Husayn Bayqara; the Musalla Complex; the poet and statesman Mir Ali-Shir Nava'i; the painter Behzad
f.today: Herat is the capital of Herat Province and the third-largest city of Afghanistan, with an estimated 673,273 settled residents.
